subject: Territorial anchoring commitment and exception playbook
messages:
From: Sam Tucker <sam.tucker@novamed.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>, dpo@novamed.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Territorial anchoring requirement + temporary exception scenarios

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the call earlier. As mentioned, NovaMed needs a written statement of your territorial anchoring guarantees for PHI-derived inference traffic, plus an operational playbook that describes exactly what happens during temporary cross-region processing (e.g., failover to another region, transient cache syncs, or third-party subprocessors).

Two specific asks to help legal/security sign off:
1) Can you confirm whether Redwood will assert "territorial anchoring" for our account (i.e., traffic will be pinned to the US region with transient exceptions limited to X hours and logged)?
2) For temporary exceptions, we need:
   - What triggers a cross-region hop (capacity, outage, maintenance)?
   - Maximum expected duration and SLA for notification.
   - Which subprocessors (names/locations) may process data during an exception window.

I've attached our questionnaire and a short list of scenarios we want covered. If you can provide a single PDF playbook we can attach to the DPA addendum that would be ideal.

Would love to have a draft by EOD Wednesday so we can loop legal.

Best,
Sam Tucker
Head of Security Programs
NovaMed Health

Attachments: nova_med_questionnaire_responses.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodai.com>

Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>, dpo@novamed.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Territorial anchoring requirement + temporary exception scenarios

Sam —

Thanks for the clear asks and the questionnaire. We can provide a formal "Territorial Anchoring Commitment" plus an operational exception playbook. High-level answers here and I'll attach the formal playbook (PDF) in a follow-up.

Quick answers:
- Commitment: we can anchor NovaMed traffic to the US region for inference and storage at-rest. We will document the scope (API routes + model versions) and provide evidence controls for audit.
- Exception triggers: automated failover (region outage), scheduler-driven maintenance, or capacity-driven autoscale policies.
- Maximum duration: by default we limit transient cross-region hops to 72 hours; for NovaMed we can contractually reduce to 24 hours with notification commitments.
- Notification: we will send a written incident/exception notice to your security distribution within 1 hour of a planned maintenance that may trigger cross-region processing; unplanned failovers will have a 4-hour initial notification followed by remediation updates.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide a roster (names + country) and a map of which subprocessors may handle ephemeral caching or telemetry during exceptions.

I've looped in Marissa (Legal Ops) and Irene (Product Ops) to draft the PDF playbook and the subprocessor roster.

Irene / Marissa — please see the questionnaire attached and draft a playbook that includes: scope, triggers, duration limits, notification cadence, key management/escrow options, and logging/audit artifacts we will provide. If we can include a short runbook example (timeline + sample notification text) that will help legal.

I'll aim to circulate the PDF by COB Wednesday.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Subject: RE: Territorial anchoring requirement + temporary exception scenarios

Thanks Sam — attaching the draft playbook and a proposed subprocessor roster for your review. Key contractual points we propose to include in the DPA addendum:

- Territorial anchoring: Redwood will keep inference requests and derived embeddings for NovaMed in the US region.
- Exception window: transient cross-region processing may occur only under the enumerated triggers, capped at 24 hours by default; extended windows require pre-approval and will be logged with justification.
- Notification/SLAs: Planned events: 72-hour notice where practical; immediate events: 4-hour initial notice and 24-hour remediation updates.
- Subprocessor transparency: Redwood will provide names, jurisdictions, and roles; for any new subprocessors we will provide 30-day notice and a chance to object where required by regulation (we can model this for healthcare customers).
- Key management: keys remain customer-scoped; for long-lived cross-region processing customers can opt into escrowed key rotation with explicit contractual terms.

Please see the attached playbook (redwood_territorial_anchoring_playbook_v1.pdf) — it contains a sample incident timeline and a template notification that NovaMed legal can paste into the DPA addendum.

Sam/Elena — open questions for you:
1) Do you need the exceptions limited to certain instance types or model classes (e.g., not allowed for PHI-annotated fine-tuned models)?
2) Do you require a signed attestation for each failover event (we can provide an automated PDF export with logs)?

If you want, we can set a 30-minute review call tomorrow to walk through the playbook and the logo-stamped DPA language.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts and Privacy
Redwood Inference
